SOURCE: Union postale universelle, Bureau international, "Dictionnaire des bureaux de poste"
        (Lausanne: Imprimeries réunies). Internet Archive item dictionnairedesb00univ.
        NOT lending-restricted. Full djvu text (12.4 MB) downloaded and searched 2026-09-06.
        "Kanawana" occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the whole file, at djvu-text line 908066.

THE ITEM CONTAINS TWO PUBLICATIONS BOUND TOGETHER, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT:

  1. The DICTIONNAIRE proper, NOVEMBRE 1909. Its own Observations, at line 100:
       OBSERVATIONS 
       i°)05 
       1.  Le  présent  Dictionnaire  contient  les  noms  des  bu- 
       reaux de  poste  de  tous  les  pays  faisant  partie  de  l'Union 
       postale  universelle,  à  la  date  du  1er  mars  1909  (à  l'excep- 

  2. A SUPPLÉMENT, AOÛT 1912. Its Observations, at line 885050:
       1 .  Le  présent  Supplément  contient  les  changements  au 
       Dictionnaire  des  bureaux  de  poste  (édition  de  novembre 
       1909)  qui  ont  été  notifiés  au  Bureau  international  par 
       les  divers  Offices  de  l'Union  et  par  l'Office  chinois  depuis 
       la  publication  de  cet  ouvrage  jusqu'au  1er  juin  1912. 
       Il  contient  également  les  noms  des  bureaux  de  poste 
       de  la  République  de  Panama  qui  ne  figurent  pas  dans 
       le  Dictionnaire. 
       2.  Ce  Supplément  se  divise  en  trois  parties,  savoir: 
       I.  Bureaux  à  ajouter  (pages  1  à  93). 
       II.  Bureaux  à  biffer  (pages  94  à  143). 
       III.  Modifications  (pages  144  à  191). 

KANAWANA IS IN THE 1912 SUPPLEMENT, PART I ("Bureaux à ajouter"), NOT IN THE 1909 DICTIONARY.
  Verified by line number: the last "Bureaux à ajouter" heading before the entry is at line
  907856, and the first "Bureaux à biffer" heading is at 944546. The entry at 908066 therefore
  sits inside Part I, offices to be ADDED.

=== THE ENTRY, name column (line 908066) ===
Kamuti  V,  m*  C    . 
Kanada  V,  M,  C     . 
Kanawana  c 
Kanawyer  c 
Kanaya  V,  M,  C     . 
Kancha  V,  C     .     . 
Kanchausi  V,  m*,  C 

=== THE COUNTRY COLUMN, which the OCR prints as a separate run below the names ===
Hawaï  (Poss.  amer.) . 
Inde  brit.,  Ramnad. 
Japon,  Buzen. 
Canada,  Québec. 
E.-U.  d'Am.,  Cal. 
Japon,  Kazusa. 
Inde  brit.,  Pindi. 
Inde  brit.,  Etawah. 

HOW THE COLUMNS WERE ALIGNED, and the check that validates it:
  Counting back from the end of both runs --
     Kanchen   <- Chine, Chekiang.
     Kanchausi <- Inde brit., Etawah.
     Kancha    <- Inde brit., Pindi.
     Kanaya    <- Japon, Kazusa.
     KANAWYER  <- E.-U. d'Am., Cal.
     KANAWANA  <- CANADA, QUÉBEC.
     Kanada    <- Japon, Buzen.
  The check is KANAWYER: it is a real place in California (Kings Canyon), which is what the
  alignment assigns it. If the offset were wrong by one, Kanawyer would land in Canada and
  Kanawana in the United States.

WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES:
  The Kanawana post office did NOT exist on 1 March 1909, the date to which the main
  dictionary is compiled, and DID exist by 1 June 1912, the closing date of the supplement.
  Opening therefore falls in that window. The YMCA bought the Saint-Sauveur site in 1910.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the exact opening date, the postmaster, or whether the office was
  the camp's own. The letter beside the name in the name column is a service code whose legend
  was not read.

THE TRAP, recorded because it nearly worked: the Internet Archive catalogues this item as
  "1909". Read at face value, a Kanawana post office in 1909 would predate the YMCA's arrival
  and unsettle the account of how the place got its name. It is in the 1912 supplement.
